The reported degradation may be ~5-10% under-stated or over-stated relative to a fully-trained step-10k adapter; cannot disambiguate without retraining or recovering the lost ckpt.

Adapter base mismatch: HF adapter_config.json declares base = meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, but we composed onto meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B (non-Instruct, BG-Ο anchor). LoRA weights were trained against Instruct's chat-templated representations; applying them to base may amplify the apparent degradation due to template-mismatch artifacts. A clean re-eval would either (a) compose LoRA onto Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct (and re-run base anchors on Instruct), or (b) retrain LoRA on non-Instruct base.

Verdict-compute c3_check awk function had unescaped double-quote bug in initial emit (PASS|/FAIL| string literals collided with outer awk "BEGIN{...}" quotes), causing c3 to evaluate as empty-string→FAIL for all 3 benches in the auto-emitted verdict.json. Fixed manually post-hoc by recomputing from per-bench JSONs (which were correctly synced). The c3 logic itself is sound; only the bash emit had the escaping bug. Future cycle should use `awk -v` to pass values rather than string interpolation.

TriviaQA filter = remove_whitespace (lm-eval default). Llama base anchor used same filter (BG-Ο). Any normalization mismatch between LoRA inference and base inference would inflate the EM delta — but since both used same filter, the 9.4pp drop is filter-consistent.

BG-Ξ amendment criterion 4 random baselines: HellaSwag/MMLU random=0.25, TriviaQA random≈0. Adding +5pp gives 0.30/0.30/0.05 thresholds. LoRA passes all 3 (0.642/0.530/0.302). c4 confirms LoRA is NOT a complete weight collapse (e.g., random/zero output) — it's a meaningful but degraded model.
